_comment: THE DERIVED PLANE'S SHAPES, declared once. Everything here lives under
.fux/runtime/ -- gitignored, disposable, rebuildable from the committed
WHY A DERIVED PLANE NEEDS A SCHEMA AT ALL, given it is disposable: because
disposable is not the same as harmless. The accelerator must return
byte-identical results to the reference scan (the differential law), so a
shape that drifts does not corrupt the index -- it makes ONE OF THE TWO
PATHS DISAGREE, which is a fast wrong answer.
That is not hypothetical. On 2026-08-23 `superseded` and `mtime` were added
to the doc table while RUNTIME_SCHEMA stayed put, so an accelerator built
minutes earlier kept being read: `ask --scan` applied a supersession
demotion and `ask --fast` did not. DOCS_FIELDS exists because of that day.
This file is the same idea, extended to the shapes that had no such guard.
IT COVERS THE WHOLE PLANE, NOT JUST POSTINGS, and that is deliberate: the
four shapes are written by one build, read by one query path, and versioned
by one string. Splitting them into four files would invite three of them to
be updated and the fourth forgotten -- which is precisely the failure mode

_doc: One line of .fux/runtime/postings/<xx>.jsonl -- term-major, the shape the
accelerator reads. `xx` is the term hash's first byte, mirroring the
committed shard addressing.
A block holds at most BLOCK_SIZE postings. Splitting is what lets the
block-max bound skip a whole run of documents without decoding them.
The tf array is PER FIELD and its length is the number of fields the
document actually uses -- trailing zeros are trimmed, which is why the
example below shows arrays of 1, 2 and 3 rather than always 5.

docidx.doc: row in docs.jsonl, ascending within a block

tf_per_field.doc: body, heading, title, path, ctx -- trailing zeros trimmed

_doc: One fixed-width record of .fux/runtime/postings/<xx>.idx -- a binary side
table, NOT a JSONL retreat. Reading a block's max impact by string-slicing
the block line measured 397ms -> 44ms; a struct.unpack at a computed index
is strictly cheaper and leaves the block line honestly valid JSON.
Entries are sorted by (term, block_no), so a term's blocks are one bisect
and then a contiguous run.
WAS 40 BYTES until W-76 Phase 1. `mx` and `mnw` were single WEIGHTED
scalars, and a weighted extremum cannot be stored once when the weights
are query-time tune keys -- it would go stale the moment someone edited
tune.toml, and only on the accelerator path, which is a differential-law
break rather than a slow query. They are now per-field and UNWEIGHTED,
recombined at the query's own weights by `accel.block_bound`.

fields.name: block_no
fields.doc: block ordinal within the term, from 0

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: byte offset of the block line in its postings shard

fields.name: length
fields.doc: byte length of the block line, newline excluded

fields.name: mx
fields.doc: per-field MAX unweighted tf in the block

fields.name: mnw
fields.doc: per-field MIN flen in the block

_why_both_extrema: A term's BM25F contribution is increasing in weighted tf AND decreasing
in flen, so an upper bound over a block needs the maximum of the first
and the minimum of the second. `mx` alone is valid but loose.
Per-field extrema OVER-estimate mx and UNDER-estimate mnw relative to the
true weighted extremum, and both errors push the bound UP -- so a block
that could contain a winner is never skipped. Measured cost: +0.0% blocks
scanned, because 92.5% of postings are single-field, which makes the
per-field sum exact rather than loose.

_doc: One line of .fux/runtime/docs.jsonl -- the docidx-ordered table every
other derived structure joins against. Line N is docidx N.
THE FIELD SET IS PART OF THE RUNTIME CONTRACT and `is_fresh` checks it.
A schema string only moves when someone remembers to move it; this field
set moves whenever the table does, because it IS the table.

title.doc: display title, or the labelled hash for a hashed record

flen.doc: per-field token counts, trailing zeros trimmed

mtime.doc: git commit time -- NOT wall clock at build time

_doc: The whole of .fux/runtime/stats.json -- the corpus-wide numbers BM25F
length normalization reads.
`total_flen` is RAW and per-field. It was a single pre-weighted
`total_wlen` until 2026-08-24: once field weights became tune.toml keys, a
weighted total stored here would move `avg_wlen` on the scan path and not
on the accelerator path. Storing raw and weighting at query time is what
keeps the two paths equal.

newest_mtime.doc: max mtime, for the recency prior
